$comment:
Canonical idempotency-digest parity corpus, v0.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.
The cross-language byte anchor for the idempotency payload hash was previously
asserted as a duplicated string literal in two places -- one in the Python
suite, one in the Node suite. Two literals that must agree, with nothing
causing them to agree, is a break waiting to happen: an edit to one side leaves
the other green and the divergence is discovered by a customer, not by CI.

This file is the single source both implementations read, following the pattern
already proven by filter_parity.v0.json. There is now exactly one place where
the expected digest is written down.

WHAT THE CANONICAL FORM IS.
A SHA-256 over a JSON array of the idempotency-significant fields, in this
order, with the three list fields sorted and with no whitespace between tokens:

  [function, purpose, sorted(scope), sorted(denyFields), sorted(blockedFields), mode]

Python uses separators=(",", ":") so that json.dumps matches JSON.stringify
byte for byte. schema_version is deliberately NOT part of this hash: it is
record metadata, so stamping it must never change the digest nor break parity.
Cases 2 and 3 exercise the sorting normalisation; cases 4 through 7 pin that
each remaining component actually participates in the digest, so a canonical
form that silently dropped a field could not pass.

BOTH SIDES MUST CALL THE REAL FUNCTION.
Each implementation feeds these inputs to its own production hash function and
compares against `expected_digest`. A test that re-derives the canonical form
inline and hashes its own reconstruction proves only that SHA-256 is
deterministic -- it stays green while the shipped function drifts underneath it.
The corpus runner must therefore reach the module's actual hash, not a local
restatement of what it is believed to do.
canonical_form: JSON array [function, purpose, sorted(scope), sorted(denyFields), sorted(blockedFields), mode], no whitespace between tokens

cases.doc: The historical byte anchor, inputs already in sorted order. This exact digest was previously duplicated as a literal in both suites; it is now written once, here.
scope supplied out of order must normalise to the anchor digest — argument order is not idempotency-significant.
denyFields and blockedFields supplied out of order likewise normalise to the anchor digest.
All three list fields empty — the degenerate shape must still be stable across languages.
mode participates in the digest: the anchor payload under FULL must not collide with it under LITE.
